To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new JAK 2V617F positive clone emerged during post-imatinib therapy in a patient with CML, who subsequently developed overt polycythema vera.
the development of a new J2K617F-positive clone and the emergence of overt PV in a patient with CML were observed after years of imatinib therapy.

a JAK2V 617F clone was detected in a patient with BCR-ABLL-positive CML after 10 years of successful imatinib treatment, and the emergence of the JAK 2V617F mutant clone was followed by clinical manifestations consistent with the diagnosis of PV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new J2K617F clone in a patient with CML, as a result of imatinib treatment, followed by the emergence of PV.
the development of a new J2K617F clone in patients with CML and the subsequent development of overt PV.
the development of CML and the acquisition of BCL-2 in patients with a prior history of PV (2-5), essential thromboembolism (5), or primary myelodysplasia (6).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
JAK2 mutation is not the cause of MPN, but rather a marker of the MPN clone.
the JAK2 mutation was not detected in the patient at the time of CML diagnosis, which suggests the JAK2-positive clone emerged later.
the BCR-AML1 and the JAK2 V617F clone are not mutually exclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patient’s JAK2V616F-positive clone was present at a low level at diagnosis, was undetectable during treatment with imatinib for CML, and emerged during the follow-up period.
the patient had CML and PV, but the PV was not diagnosed until 9.5 years after the CML diagnosis.
the development of PV in our patient was a result of clonal evolution and that imatinib therapy was not a causative factor for PV.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a JAK2V 617F clone, which can be detected by quantitative JAK2V616F mutation analysis, in the BM or peripheral blood of a patient with CML, ET or PV should not preclude the use of imatinib therapy in the treatment of BCR-AB1-positive disease, as long as the JAK2 mutation is not dominant in terms of allele burden.
, despite the presence of a BCR- ABL1 clone for over 9 years, the emergence of a JAK2V-617F clone and the subsequent development of overt PV in our patient was not anticipated.
JAK2 inhibition might be a reasonable therapeutic approach for patients with CML and JAK2 mutation, as it has been for patients with JAK2V6-17F-positive MPN (23–25).
